ci_method: OLS of outcome on treatment plus all 12 pre-treatment covariates (continuous terms linear, region/education/employment as factors), HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust SEs, 95% t-interval. Pre-specified as primary. Agrees with: unadjusted Welch diff-in-means 0.134 [0.058,0.211]; Lin (2013) fully-interacted centered-covariate estimator 0.132 [0.064,0.201]; nonparametric bootstrap (2,000 reps) [0.059,0.204]; causal-forest AIPW 0.133 [0.064,0.202]; randomization-inference p=0.0006.
specifications_run: A. Unadjusted difference in means, Welch t-interval: +0.134 [0.058, 0.211], p=0.0006
B. OLS outcome~treat, HC2 robust SEs (no covariates): +0.134 [0.058, 0.211]
C. PRIMARY: OLS outcome~treat + all 12 baseline covariates, HC2: +0.132 [0.064, 0.200], p=0.00015
D. Lin (2013) estimator: treat interacted with all mean-centered covariates, HC2: +0.132 [0.064, 0.201]
E. Randomization inference (10,000 permutations of treatment) on unadjusted diff: two-sided p=0.0006
F. Nonparametric bootstrap (2,000 resamples) of covariate-adjusted ATE: [0.059, 0.204]
G. Mann-Whitney U rank test (distribution-free): p=0.0010
H. HETEROGENEITY omnibus: joint Wald test of all 17 treat x covariate interactions = 0: F=1.19, p=0.266 (NULL)

I. HETEROGENEITY per-covariate interaction tests, 17 terms, with Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni correction: smallest raw p=0.039 (education='Some college'), smallest BH-adjusted p=0.418, smallest Bonferroni p=0.66 -> none survive (NULL)

J. DISCARDED AS INVALID: naive within-subgroup ATEs for 29 subgroups (4 binary x2, 11 category levels, 5 median splits x2). 17 of 29 had p<0.05, but these test 'ATE=0 inside this subgroup', NOT 'this subgroup differs from others' -- with a true common effect of +0.13 most subgroups are individually significant by construction. Reported for transparency only; not used for any heterogeneity claim.

K. HETEROGENEITY correct form: 12 formal difference-in-ATE (interaction) tests, one per covariate, HC2, with BH/Bonferroni: smallest raw p=0.107 (mobile_primary), region p=0.132, education p=0.159; no BH-adjusted p below 0.40 (NULL)
L. Causal forest (grf, 4,000 trees, known propensity 0.5), AIPW ATE: +0.133 (SE 0.035)

M. HETEROGENEITY omnibus: Chernozhukov et al. best-linear-predictor calibration test on held-out data: mean.forest.prediction=0.993 (p<0.001, ATE well calibrated) but differential.forest.prediction=-2.44, one-sided p=0.999 -> forest finds no real signal in CATE variation (NULL)
N. Causal-forest variable importance (income_k, age, baseline_score, tenure top-ranked) -- splitting pattern consistent with noise, not corroborated by any honest test
O. Best linear projection of forest CATE on all covariates: only education='Some college' has raw p<0.05 (0.038) out of 17 terms; fails multiplicity correction (NULL)

P. HETEROGENEITY honest out-of-sample: RATE/AUTOC, CATE ranking fit on one random half, evaluated on the other: -0.018 (SE 0.051), p=0.73 -- targeting the program by predicted CATE yields no gain over treating everyone (NULL)

Q. HETEROGENEITY family-wise: permutation null for the maximum |interaction t| across all 12 covariates (500 re-randomizations): observed max t=2.37 vs null mean 2.22 and 95th pct 3.11, family-wise p=0.33 -- the single most extreme apparent subgroup difference (West region, raw p=0.018) is exactly what the search produces by chance
R. Power/MDE for heterogeneity: SE on a binary-split difference-in-ATE is ~0.08, so MDE at 80% power is ~0.22 SD; West-vs-rest MDE ~0.26 SD
S. Region-level homogeneity test (4 regions jointly): F=1.87, p=0.132 (NULL)

T. Overall-ATE robustness: outcome winsorized at 1/99 (+0.134); dropping top 1% of income_k (+0.124); log(income) specification (+0.133); SEs clustered by region (+0.132 [0.059,0.205]); HC1 and HC3 SEs (identical to 3 decimals) -- all stable
U. Quantile treatment effects at deciles 10/25/50/75/90: +0.16, +0.14, +0.12, +0.10, +0.16 -- near-uniform location shift, no evidence of effects concentrated in part of the distribution
assumptions_checked: Randomization/covariate balance: exactly 1,200 per arm; standardized mean differences for all 9 numeric+binary covariates are |SMD|<=0.09 (all well under 0.1); chi-square tests for region (p=0.33), education (p=0.90), employment (p=0.85). Two covariates have raw p<0.10 (sessions_prior_30d p=0.033, female p=0.060); with 12 tests this is expected under pure chance, and the ATE is unchanged when they are adjusted for (0.134 -> 0.132), so the imbalance is immaterial.
Missing data / attrition: zero missing cells in all 15 columns, no duplicate participant_ids, exact 50/50 arm sizes -> no differential attrition and no need for attrition bounds or imputation.
SUTVA / no interference: not testable from this file; assumed, as is standard for an individually randomized program. Noted as an assumption rather than a verified fact.

Outcome distribution: residual skew 0.03, excess kurtosis 0.01, Jarque-Bera p=0.84 -> approximately normal; results also confirmed by distribution-free Mann-Whitney and by randomization inference, so no reliance on normality.
Homoskedasticity: Levene test across arms p=0.93, Breusch-Pagan on the adjusted model p=0.61. HC2 robust SEs used regardless; HC1/HC3/cluster variants give identical intervals.
Influential observations: maximum Cook's distance 0.010 (far below the ~1 threshold); income_k has a right tail to 303k, and dropping the top 1% moves the estimate only 0.132 -> 0.124.

Functional form: additive-linear covariate specification compared against the fully interacted Lin estimator and a nonparametric causal forest; all three ATEs agree to within 0.001, so the ATE is not an artifact of the covariate functional form.

Multiplicity in the subgroup search: the 29 candidate subgroups / 12 covariates were corrected via Benjamini-Hochberg, Bonferroni, and a family-wise permutation null for the maximum interaction t-statistic. This is the decisive check -- it is what separates the 17 'significant' naive subgroup results from the zero genuine heterogeneity findings.

Overfitting of the heterogeneity model: guarded against with honest sample splitting -- the Chernozhukov calibration test on held-out data and the RATE/AUTOC with CATE ranking trained on an independent half. Both are null, confirming the in-sample forest splits reflect noise.

Power to detect heterogeneity: explicitly computed. At n=2,400 the minimum detectable difference between two halves of the sample is ~0.22 SD, i.e. larger than the overall effect itself. So the null heterogeneity result rules out large differential effects but cannot rule out modest ones -- stated as a limitation rather than claimed as proof of exact uniformity.
headline_claim: The onboarding program raised eight-week engagement by 0.13 standard deviations (95% CI 0.06 to 0.20, p<0.001), and this benefit appears uniform across participants -- no subgroup was reliably more or less affected once we accounted for the number of subgroups tested, though the trial can only rule out differential effects larger than about 0.22 SD.
